topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, contextualizes the lecture within the course, and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Determinants of Cancer Risk: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological definition of cancer and evaluate the relative contributions of intrinsic cellular processes, environmental exposures, public perception, and geographic epidemiological variation to cancer development.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how bacterial, parasitic, and viral infections contribute to oncogenesis, illustrated through the detailed epidemiological and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary toxins, UV radiation, and environmental chemicals undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Initiator-Promoter Models, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic promoters, experimental models distinguishing initiation from promotion, host developmental vulnerabilities, and provide an integrative summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the range of experimental and analytical approaches used to demonstrate carcinogenicity, including mutational signature sequencing, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo models, and in vitro assays.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Decision Making and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic summarises the lecture and considers the practical balance between environmental risks and daily benefits.
